title: Where The Holy People Constantly Vibrate
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 256
summary: This shabad opens with where the Holy people constantly vibrate the Kirtan of the Praises of the Lord. It turns the heart toward the Righteous Judge says, ""Do not approach that place, O Messenger of Death.
whyItMatters: It matters when life feels sharp, loose-tongued, and careless because the shabad keeps speech inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private momentum.
takeaway: Keep returning to this turn: the Righteous Judge says, ""Do not approach that place, O Messenger of Death.

lines.gurmukhi: ਜਹ ਸਾਧੂ ਗੋਬਿਦ ਭਜਨੁ ਕੀਰਤਨੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਨੀਤ ॥
lines.transliteration: jeh saadhoo gobidh bhajan keeratan naanak neet ||
lines.translation: Where the Holy people constantly vibrate the Kirtan of the Praises of the Lord of the Universe, O Nanak

lines.gurmukhi: ਣਾ ਹਉ ਣਾ ਤੂੰ ਣਹ ਛੁਟਹਿ ਨਿਕਟਿ ਨ ਜਾਈਅਹੁ ਦੂਤ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naa hau naa too(n) neh chhuTeh nikaT na jaieeahu dhoot ||1||
lines.translation: - the Righteous Judge says, ""Do not approach that place, O Messenger of Death, or else neither you nor I shall escape!""||1||

structure: It opens by naming the condition without ornament: where the Holy people constantly vibrate the Kirtan of the Praises of the Lord.
The middle movement widens the correction through the Righteous Judge says, ""Do not approach that place, O Messenger of Death.
It closes with a return you can actually keep: the Righteous Judge says, ""Do not approach that place, O Messenger of Death.
